verdict.rationale: Base44 documents real code export: the CLI `eject` command downloads an app's frontend code and backend resources into a separate local project, and GitHub sync lets you keep the code in your own repository. However, the ejected project gets a new Base44 app ID and the SDK positions Base44 as the backend service, so there is no evidence the app can run or be hosted fully independent of the platform. Missing for 10: documented self-hosting or deployment outside Base44, a portable backend and database that runs off-platform, and hands-on corroboration that exported code runs independently.

support.subject: As a developer, I can export the full source code and run or host the app outside the platform

citations.quote: Clone an existing Base44 app into a separate local project. This command downloads the frontend code and backend resources from a selected app and creates a new project with its own app ID.
Connect your Base44 app to GitHub for version control, local development, and collaboration.
Use the SDK to build your own frontend or backend that uses Base44 as a backend service.
